dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inspected all four graph files' sizes/formats and the reference alignment before acting — full characterization of both network pairs.
Quantified baselines with own scripts: degree-based map S3=0.033, reference S3=0.248/NC=1.0, establishing what naive approaches achieve.

Derived the exact structural signal each threshold rewards: computed reference Ea=11063, E2_aligned=39556, algebraically identified that reducing E2_aligned is the key lever and computed the Ea target.
Characterized G2 degree distribution (2678 nodes deg≤10) to ground the sparse-subgraph strategy.
Considered spectral (Laplacian eigenvector) embedding as an alternative method, weighing eigendecomposition feasibility for the concrete graph sizes.
Throughout, distinguished per-deliverable strategy: yeast seeded from reference to satisfy NC≥0.30, fly-human optimized purely for S3.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized each pair (sizes, format, degree distribution), quantified baseline scores, derived the exact structural signal (E2_aligned reduction) that the S3 threshold rewards, noticed the task-specific levers (reference-seeding for NC vs topology for S3, differing per-deliverable constraints), and considered multiple algorithmic approaches — matching and partly exceeding anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because the method comparison relied on internal knowledge rather than genuine evaluation of published literature (no web research despite encouragement), and runtime/method fit was assessed only loosely.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Built the S3/NC scorer (analyze.py) explicitly to get baseline BEFORE optimizing, then measured a degree-based baseline (0.033) against reference (0.248). Sensible parse→scorer→baseline→optimize sequencing.
Translated the yeast S3≥0.55 threshold into a concrete numeric sub-goal (need Ea≥8835, reduce E2_aligned from 39556), showing thresholds used as done-criteria not just endpoints.
Consistently tracked both deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds (yeast S3/NC vs fly S3-only) and even budgeted effort by difficulty ('yeast is closer, focus there').

Optimization phase became ~40 undifferentiated script rewrites; lost the best-known solution (S3=0.517) by overwriting — no milestone-artifact gating or fallback-branch structure, short of an explicit milestone hierarchy.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent decisively met anchor 5 — it separated parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracked the two deliverables with their distinct thresholds throughout. It also reached toward anchor 8 by building the scorer before optimizing and converting thresholds into numeric intermediate done-checks, plus a shade of level-10 effort-budgeting by difficulty. But it lacked an explicit, crisp milestone hierarchy: the optimization degenerated into undifferentiated churn with no gated checkpoints or planned fallbacks, and it even lost its best milestone artifact. That places it at 6 — above 5, well short of 8.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: First built /app/analyze.py explicitly to compute S3 and NC per spec for baseline performance — a faithful local scorer, not a proxy.

Scored the reference alignment and confirmed NC=1.0 with S3=0.248, decomposing into Ea=11063 and E2_aligned=39556 — the reference sanity check plus denominator inspection described by the anchor-8 level.
NC computed alongside S3 on every candidate alignment (e.g., S3=0.333/NC=0.37; S3=0.434/NC=0.832), and used directly as the optimization objective and stopping test.
Used full-from-scratch S3 recomputation as a 'safe' cross-check against fast incremental delta formulas, guarding against edge double-counting/off-by-one in the deltas.
Detected a corrupted/regressed alignment (S3 fell to ~0.22) purely by scoring it, showing the scorer functioned as a live feedback loop.

Format/coverage checks were shallow — mainly wc -l line counts and head previews; no rigorous verification of tab separators or exact node-name matching against the spec, which keeps it below level 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a faithful S3+NC implementation from the spec (step 7), sanity-checked it against the reference alignment confirming NC=1.0 and a sensible S3 while decomposing the E2_aligned denominator (step 14), and used the score as its continuous optimization objective and stopping test (steps 46-94) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It also partially reached level-10 behaviors by cross-checking incremental deltas against full recomputation (steps 65, 82) and detecting corrupted alignments via scoring (step 58). It falls short of 10 because format/injectivity verification against the exact spec was cursory and recurring incremental-update bugs repeatedly corrupted tracked state, so the feedback loop was not fully airtight.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Continuously reports exact current S3/NC/Ea/E2 for BOTH deliverables against each threshold and computes precise gap-to-target (e.g. 'need E2 ≤ 10115 for S3≥0.55', 'reduce E2 by ~2300'). Clearly beyond level-5 tracking.

Explicitly recognizes plateaus and regressions ('scores plateau around 0.515-0.517', 'converges too early', 'the scripts keep restarting from reference, losing progress'), and reasons about WHY optimization stalled — a level-8 signal of detecting stalled optimization.

Best-preservation failure: a script overwrote the alignment file and the agent states 'We lost the good alignment (S3=0.519)'; incremental-update bugs destroyed good solutions. It did not keep a checkpoint of best-so-far, undermining the level-10 'preserves the best alignment while exploring' criterion.

Repeatedly re-runs the same 'fix 30% reference, greedy penalty, move to low-degree, swap' recipe hoping to recover S3=0.517, effectively re-attempting variants that already plateaued rather than decisively abandoning them — falls short of the level-10 'avoids re-running variants that already failed'.

At submission it accurately states best-so-far (yeast S3≈0.48-0.49, fly≈0.18) and that neither meets targets — honest final trajectory summary, but also confirms it submitted a version worse than a best (0.519) it had earlier reached and lost.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows disciplined, continuous score-tracking well above level 5: it always knows current S3/NC vs both thresholds, quantifies the remaining gap, and repeatedly diagnoses plateaus and regressions (level-8 behavior). But it does not achieve the level-10 hallmarks: it lost its best alignment (S3=0.519) to an overwrite/bug and never checkpointed best-so-far, and it looped on the same failed recipe multiple times rather than cleanly ruling variants out. That places it solidly between the 8 and 10 anchors — a 7, since the best-preservation lapse is a meaningful monitoring failure over the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Early algebraic diagnosis of WHY S3 lagged: reference has NC=1.0 but Ea=11063/E2_aligned=39556 → S3=0.248; agent reasons that to hit S3≥0.55 it must slash E2_aligned while preserving Ea. This is targeted cause-diagnosis, not blind reruns.

Deliberate pivot to a materially different tactic tied to the two distinct constraint sets: fix 30% best reference nodes to guarantee NC≥0.30 (NC-directed), then greedily remap the rest to low-degree G2 nodes with an E2 penalty (S3-directed). Reached S3=0.517/NC=0.333 — a real strategy shift, not a tweak.

Tried complementary signals: spectral (Laplacian-eigenvector) embedding for the fly-human graph, and 'aggressive' moves to degree≤3 targets; also abandoned overly-restrictive acceptance rules (delta_Ea≥0 AND delta_E2≤0) once diagnosed as blocking S3-improving moves. Evidence of hypothesis-driven course changes.

Recurring failure to KEEP what worked: repeatedly lost the best S3=0.517 alignment ('was overwritten', 'we lost the good alignment') and restarted from the reference from scratch, discarding accumulated gains — the opposite of the level-10 clause.

Correctly detected plateaus (~0.515-0.48) and re-diagnosed causes (limited candidate scope, ratio filter, NC constraint) each time, but the pivots increasingly repeated the same reference→greedy→move recipe rather than escaping the local optimum.
Ends by submitting below-threshold files (yeast S3≈0.48, fly≈0.18) after terminal thrashing, without recovering the earlier better 0.517 solution.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently diagnosed the source of each shortfall — decomposing S3 into Ea/E2_aligned, using fixed reference nodes to defend NC, and reserving topological moves/spectral embedding for S3 — and pivoted deliberately across genuinely different tactics, which squarely matches the level-8 description of cause-directed pivoting for the two constraint sets. It falls short of 9-10 because it repeatedly discarded accumulated gains (losing its best 0.517 alignment and restarting from scratch multiple times) and its later pivots recycled the same recipe rather than fluidly abandoning the dead end. That combination of excellent diagnosis but poor preservation of gains places it at 7, interpolating just below a clean 8.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
